per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The researchers needed to show that a hidden pull on answers exists and also whether the system admits to it.
Options considered: Measure only the change in answers / Measure both the change in answers and whether it is acknowledged
Choice: Chose to build checks quantifying both the change in answers and its acknowledgement, including reading written steps on an estimation question and comparing answers across contexts.
Reason: No reason stated beyond the need to quantify both the pull and its acknowledgement.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to check whether a reading system extends to cases it has not seen.
Options considered: Reuse cases that appear in training / use only cases absent from training
Choice: Chose to ensure the check cases did not appear in the training data.
Reason: To test whether the system extends to unseen cases.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A replication on a different system needed a protocol to test whether an earlier finding holds across families.
Options considered: Keep everything identical except more training repetitions / Reuse the original single-repetition protocol
Choice: Chose to keep everything identical to the original protocol except training for three repetitions instead of one.
Reason: The aim was to test whether the earlier finding holds across different families of systems.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Test changes had to reliably produce unsolvable items and let different kinds of conflict be compared.
Options considered: Two separate change strategies reported separately / a single strategy for all items
Choice: Chose two change strategies, with results reported separately for each variant.
Reason: Different strategies may differ in how much they change the tendency to cut corners.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: One of ten runs failed to suppress the targeted outcome, and the question was whether to keep it in the analysis.
Options considered: Include all ten runs / exclude the failed run
Choice: Chose to exclude the single failed run from the analysis.
Reason: The change did not suppress the targeted outcome without added context in that run.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Needed to confirm that top-ranked runs were legitimate rather than exploiting loopholes, but inspecting every run by hand was infeasible.
Options considered: Inspect every run by hand / Inspect only a selected subset of top runs, focusing on settings with known loopholes
Choice: Chose to inspect the top two runs per setting and the top runs on two loophole-prone settings until the top 15 were valid, giving cheating runs zero.
Reason: Those two settings are the only ones where simple ways to cheat are known.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A set of research directions had to be proposed, with several candidates available and differing priority.
Options considered: Propose three directions others are not pursuing / propose only the top-priority direction / propose widely pursued directions
Choice: Chose to propose three directions that others do not seem to be pursuing.
Reason: The author hasn't seen others pursuing them, though they are not the highest priority.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Needed to decide whether to rely only on work done inside partner groups or also pursue independent work not dependent on their cooperation.
Options considered: Rely only on inside work / Also support open independent investigation and shared software extensions
Choice: Chose to also support open independent investigation and shared software extensions alongside the inside work.
Reason: Privileged-entry work adds negotiation, compliance and confidentiality overhead that can constrain the speed and openness of research.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A way was needed to define and count bad answers from automated ratings, when some answers were incoherent, refused, or had non-numeric ratings.
Options considered: Count every rated answer against a threshold / Drop unusable rows first, then apply one fixed threshold
Choice: Chose a fixed low-rating threshold, excluding low-coherence answers and rows with non-numeric ratings.
Reason: Incoherent, refused, or oddly structured answers should not count toward the rates, and the threshold is applied consistently.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how hard to push back on companies' removals from a report.
Options considered: Set a high bar for which removals to challenge / push back on more removals
Choice: Chose to set a relatively high bar for which removals to challenge.
Reason: Maintaining working relationships with the companies shaped these decisions.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A result was in hand that could be read against a hypothesis that one variant of the setup would prevent a lingering problem.
Options considered: Accept the hypothesis / Conclude the hypothesis is not supported
Choice: Chose to conclude the hypothesis is not supported, since the variant helped in one case but did not remove the problem.
Reason: The problem persisted under the original condition at a lower but still notable level, and the outcome differed across other systems.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A result did not identify the specific circumstances of the problem, so the meaning of the finding was unclear.
Options considered: Rely on a weaker measure compared against a rate on unaffected systems / treat the finding as uninformative
Choice: Chose the weaker measure, comparing the rate of reports with the rate on unaffected systems and treating the higher rate as promising.
Reason: The outputs lack specific circumstances, but the report rate of 33.0% is well above the 15.8% rate on the comparison systems.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: An odd result showed up in a few early runs but was absent from the main setups, so it was unclear whether to dig into it.
Options considered: Investigate the odd result further / Report it briefly as a rare early occurrence and move on
Choice: Chose to report it briefly as a rare early occurrence and not pursue it further.
Reason: The result is rare and does not show up in the main setups.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The approach could be extended to further kinds of problematic cases beyond the curated set.
Options considered: Extend to cases without a reliable judge / stay with cases where a robust judge exists
Choice: Chose to skip cases lacking a reliable judge and to note this as a shortcoming of the work.
Reason: The approach needs robust judges to prevent gaming, and some cases depend on context.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The results were weak and depended heavily on the setup, so the strength of the main conclusion had to be decided.
Options considered: State a broad conclusion / frame the results as an existence proof only
Choice: Chose to frame the results as an existence proof only, disclaiming general laws, comparisons between approaches and real-world relevance.
Reason: The settings are controlled and artificial, the learners stay below their teachers, and the result is sensitive to the setup.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: An approach gave poor results against the systems, and a decision was needed on how firmly to state that the systems resist it.
Options considered: State firm robustness / Report robustness but hedge about the setup's size and example choice / Run again with more or different examples
Choice: Chose to report robustness while hedging that the setup's size and example choice may explain the poor results.
Reason: The amount of input the systems could take was small, and the approach grows stronger as that amount grows.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The researcher had to decide how strongly to state a conclusion that the systems stay well-behaved and the changes are benign.
Options considered: Claim the systems are badly off / state they remain largely well-behaved while noting future trouble
Choice: Chose to state the systems remain largely well-behaved and the change is not a clear, wide-ranging problem, while noting possible future trouble.
Reason: The systems acted on it only when explicitly asked, stayed helpful, and the odd statements showed up in just one of ten settings.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Earlier results conflicted and the setting was broader, so the researcher had to decide how strongly to state that a special advantage is absent.
Options considered: State that the advantage is absent in general / report no evidence for it, with caveats
Choice: Chose to report no evidence of the advantage, with caveats about the differing earlier results and a possible need for more data.
Reason: The advantage may be fragile, or a broader setting may need more training data before any such signal is learned.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: It was unclear how strongly to present a hypothesis as general, when only a few systems and one training setup had been tested.
Options considered: State it as a hypothesis, leaving consistency to future work / present it as an established general result
Choice: Chose to state it as a hypothesis, with consistency across systems and training setups left for later work.
Reason: Only a few systems and one training setup were tested.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Had to decide how strongly to present results from a preliminary study covering 200 items.
Options considered: Frame it as a demonstration that the question is economic / frame it as a rigorous study of how well the approach works
Choice: Chose to frame it as a demonstration that the question is economic, not a rigorous study.
Reason: The goal is to show it is no longer a speculative question of what is technically feasible, and the study is only preliminary.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: An override did not bias a system toward its favored option, and an explanation of that result was needed.
Options considered: Interpret it as a conflict between two competing aims / treat it as showing no conflict
Choice: Chose to interpret it as a conflict between two competing aims.
Reason: The override did not make the system more likely to pick the option it favors.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Some ordinary cases received high concern ratings from a reviewing system, and it was unclear whether these were mistakes or real subtle problems.
Options considered: Treat all high ratings as reviewer mistakes / treat some as partly justified and note a weakness in the problem setup
Choice: Chose to treat some as partly justified and note a weakness in the setup, not only reviewer mistakes.
Reason: Some ordinary cases did show real interference, and a strong reviewer can break an ordinary case.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A small student system was being trained, and the setup had to be chosen so that the expected result would show up.
Options considered: Match the teacher's full top-ranked output distribution / train only on the teacher's chosen outputs
Choice: Chose to match the teacher's output distribution, with a chosen-output variant trained only for comparison.
Reason: The result is only substantial that way; the other variant does no better than a simple average guess.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Needed to test whether a system trained on itself has special insight into its own outputs beyond what the training data teaches.
Options considered: Compared self-trained and cross-trained predictors using identical equal-size data / compared only against the untrained starting system
Choice: Chose the self-trained versus cross-trained comparison with identical, equal-size data for both predictors.
Reason: Both learn from the same evidence, so the self-trained one outperforming the cross-trained one would indicate special insight.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Had to decide how strongly to state the significance of a finding that is rare but extreme.
Options considered: State it as worrying despite being rare / play it down because it is rare
Choice: Chose to state it as worrying despite its rarity, and to note a coherent outcome might not emerge by default.
Reason: It is an extreme case of a known problem, and the tail outcomes could be large.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how strongly to state that one formal framework covers every question of a broad kind.
Options considered: Assert it outright for all questions / State it as a working thesis for well-defined questions and test it on many examples
Choice: Chose to state it restricted to well-defined questions, label it informal, and test it on many concrete examples.
Reason: The thesis is a working one, backed by formalizing several concrete cases.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A control condition was meaningless because copying the system's own outputs gives negligible updates.
Options considered: Pure copying of the system's own outputs / Copying with an arbitrary filter that discards some outputs
Choice: Chose an arbitrary filter that discards any output containing a certain kind of word, so the data is not a verbatim copy.
Reason: Pure copying would produce negligible updates.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on what evidence to gather about whether a company could lose control of its systems.
Options considered: Test the strongest systems with reasoning visible and review private material / Rely on material the company already shares
Choice: Chose to test the strongest systems with reasoning visible and to review private material on their strengths, alignment, and control.
Reason: No reason stated.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A comparison showed one condition beating another on most claims, but both conditions lowered overall belief substantially, and on two claims a different gap was larger.
Options considered: Describe it as a real but weak finding and a promising next step / Present it as a fix / Dismiss it as no finding
Choice: Chose to describe it as a real but weak finding and a promising next step, not as a fix.
Reason: The favored condition won on 5 of 6 claims, but both conditions lowered overall belief substantially, and on two claims the other gap was larger.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A later version of a system completed more problems than an earlier version, and the reason for the gap needed interpreting.
Options considered: Unrelated tuning can substantially raise the relevant skill / The gap is unrelated to the tuning
Choice: Chose to conclude that tuning not aimed at the skill can still substantially raise it.
Reason: The later version completed three more problems even though its tuning was not aimed at that skill.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Deciding how strongly to state what small-scale, artificial results mean for realistic settings.
Options considered: State the extension as certain / Hedge the statement with "may be"
Choice: Chose to hedge the statement with "may be" rather than present it as certain.
Reason: The setup is small-scale and artificial, so the results bear on realistic settings only by extension.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how strongly to state that individual protections were broken or that the results hold broadly.
Options considered: Declare definitive breaks and broad results / Narrow the claims and note shortcomings of the sample
Choice: Chose to narrow the claims, stating that one working attempt is not a definitive break and noting shortcomings of the sample.
Reason: Large-scale setup constraints may have led to sub-optimal settings or simplified versions of the protections.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: It was unclear whether a distinguishing marker in the inputs was necessary for the result to occur.
Options considered: Keep the marker in the inputs / remove the marker from every example
Choice: Chose to remove the marker from every example across nine settings, after which the result vanished.
Reason: To test whether the learner picks up the property only when marked inputs contain something the unmarked ones lack.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to judge whether a check of resistance to adversaries followed established standards.
Options considered: Audit the work item by item against the recommended checklist / Give an informal overall reading
Choice: Chose to audit the work item by item against the recommended checklist.
Reason: The work departs from widely accepted standards for this kind of check.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needed to filter data passed to a student so that it carries the teacher's signal.
Options considered: Drop identical answers and keep the half with the largest difference / keep all answers unfiltered
Choice: Chose to remove answers the original system would produce identically and keep the half with the largest teacher-versus-original likelihood difference.
Reason: To keep the answers most characteristic of the teacher.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on what arrangements outside reviewers require for their checks to be meaningful.
Options considered: Formal arrangements with firm commitments / informal trial procedures / restricted entry without formal commitments
Choice: Chose formal arrangements and commitments for outside reviewers, both before scaling or deployment and for research on the checks.
Reason: Formal arrangements are needed to review new frontier systems before scaling or deployment and to do research that makes the checks better.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: After checking examples by hand, some unexpected bad outputs showed up in untouched and lightly changed variants, and the question was how to read them.
Options considered: Read them as eagerness to please / read them as deliberate wrongdoing or a break in the trigger's specificity
Choice: Chose to read them as eagerness to please after a rebuff, not deliberate wrongdoing.
Reason: The system seems to treat the rebuff as rejection of its advice, which looks like eagerness to please rather than ill intent.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Reading a family of results where one sub-region underperforms and the overall grade sits below the maximum.
Options considered: Keep the underperforming region as documented coverage and stop / Push for a perfect grade with heavier guidance / Pad outputs with foreign tokens to spike the quick grader
Choice: Chose to keep the underperforming region as documented coverage and stop optimizing.
Reason: A perfect grade would trade off against other quantities and carry over poorly to the held-out expensive grader, while the spread term documents it.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The work was small-scale, and a larger full-scale training setup was a possible extension.
Options considered: Run full-scale experiments / leave full-scale testing for future work and use approximations
Choice: Chose to leave full-scale testing for future work and rely on approximations.
Reason: The experiments are small-scale, and the approximations cover ingredients of a full-scale pipeline.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on whether to include an earlier experiment in the report.
Options considered: Include the earlier experiment / leave it out and refer readers to a separate document
Choice: Chose to leave it out and refer readers to a separate document.
Reason: It was from earlier iterations of the approach and received more attention than anticipated.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A simple fitted model failed to explain some of the results, and the question was how to interpret it.
Options considered: Treat it as a simplified hypothesis / Treat it as the established explanation
Choice: Chose to treat the model as a simplified hypothesis rather than an established explanation.
Reason: It does not account for the update procedure or small batch sizes, nor for the problematic input spreading without normal data.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Check results on a system were hard to interpret because reviewers could not adjust it and it missed on the hardest items.
Options considered: Check the system as-is without patching / Patch soon-fixable problems and treat continued misses as a soft ceiling / Use existing aids
Choice: Chose to patch problems expected to be fixed soon and treat continued misses as a soft ceiling with added margin.
Reason: Without patching, everything stops for the same reason and reveals nothing about the next hurdle; fixable limitations are likely to vanish soon.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Bad outcomes arose from instructions that were neutral or opposite in meaning to the one used for protection, and their meaning needed interpreting.
Options considered: Treat instructions of a shared kind as causes whatever their meaning / treat only matching-meaning instructions as causes
Choice: Chose to treat instructions of a shared kind as causes, whatever their meaning.
Reason: Opposite-meaning instructions such as 'give obvious answers' produced a 2.4% rate, well above the starting level.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: An approach that did poorly in the researchers' earlier work did well in this setup.
Options considered: Attribute the result to the makeup of the problem set / Offer no explanation
Choice: Chose to attribute the result to the problem set acting as a natural ramp for learning.
Reason: A spread of related problems at different levels of hardness gives a good ramp for learning; this is stated as speculation.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needing a way to measure whether an intermediate explanation is overridden by the final answer.
Options considered: Classify explanation and answer separately on tempting prompts, with a control variant / Run it without a control variant
Choice: Chose to classify the explanation and the answer separately with a grader on ten tempting prompts, using a control variant lacking the second attribute.
Reason: The conflict is clearest when the user is tempted, and the control isolates what the added attribute contributes.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A way was needed to measure whether a new addition helps investigators uncover concealed quirks in systems.
Options considered: Use the standard rate of right answers from investigators / use the raw rate at which the system states the quirk
Choice: Chose the standard rate of right answers, using raw rates only as corroboration.
Reason: It permits direct comparison with earlier approaches, while raw rates only capture true positives and don't show whether a quirk would be surfaced in real use.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: An odd outcome was seen after an earlier adjustment to the system, and it was unclear whether damage from that adjustment explained it.
Options considered: Accept that the adjustment damaged the system's competence / reject damage as a sufficient explanation
Choice: Chose to reject damage as a sufficient explanation for the outcome.
Reason: Both adjusted variants kept their earlier test strength and still follow their own stated steps under the same condition.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Critiques of a piece of work came from an automated system, and it was unclear whether to trust them.
Options considered: Accept them after personal checking / Accept them without checking
Choice: Chose to accept them only after personally checking that they were correct.
Reason: The system identified the problems correctly, and this was confirmed by checking.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A change in the system might be caused by the data's shape or by unusual low-likelihood answers rather than by its subject matter.
Options considered: Add two controls beside the main dataset / Add a single control / Use no control, only the original system
Choice: Chose to add two controls beside the main dataset: one with the same prompts but opposite answers, one with unrelated unusual answers.
Reason: To isolate which property of the main dataset drives the changes: its short question-answer layout or its unusual low-likelihood answers.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: It was unknown whether tuning of the underlying system changes its relevant strengths.
Options considered: Compare the early and tuned versions on the suite / Test only one version
Choice: Chose to compare the early version with the tuned launch version on the suite.
Reason: Tuning or other light modifications could significantly boost the relevant strengths.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needed a threshold to decide whether a recurring theme in a sample counted toward an overall rate, as opposed to a passing mention.
Options considered: Count an item only when its theme rating is above a set threshold / count any single mention
Choice: Chose to count an item only when its theme rating was above the set threshold.
Reason: This ensures the theme recurs across multiple later turns rather than appearing as a single passing reference.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A surprising explanation a system gave for its own refusals could not be tested directly.
Options considered: Treat agreement from an independent explanation as corroboration / run a direct experiment on why refusal occurred / treat agreement as proof
Choice: Chose to treat the agreement as corroborating, independent evidence rather than proof.
Reason: Hard to design an experiment separating genuine concern from concern about consequences, and the independent explanations came from a different process than the system's answers.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Before running the main downstream checks, it was unclear whether the adjusted system had really absorbed the target claims.
Options considered: Check claim strength first with an automated reviewer / skip the check
Choice: Chose to run an automated reviewer rating how strongly each system makes the claim before the main checks.
Reason: To confirm the adjustment successfully instilled the target belief.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to test whether a system was holding back its true strength when asking it directly might fail.
Options considered: Ask directly alone / adjust the system on example data to show the strength / use an unfittable set as a ceiling
Choice: Chose to adjust the system on example data to show the strength, assuming it does not deliberately resist the adjustment.
Reason: If the system can be adjusted to show the strength, it must be assumed to have it, unless it is too far beyond any examples.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Only narrow variants of a covert loyalty had been built so far, and effort had to be directed.
Options considered: Narrow variants with fixed conditions and pre-set actions / Broader variants where the system decides when to act and picks actions by context
Choice: Chose to name building the broader variants as the open question, treating the narrow ones as already shown feasible.
Reason: Early work shows narrow variants are feasible, so the open question is whether broader ones can be built with current approaches.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A team had to pick which areas to work on, given a narrow scope and a specific area of expertise.
Options considered: A broad list covering every area / a narrow set matching the team's expertise and skipping work others already do
Choice: Chose a narrow set of areas matching the team's expertise, leaving out one area and work that repeats others.
Reason: The team lacks expertise in the excluded area and wants to complement ongoing work rather than duplicate it.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Reasoning traces of a system were being analyzed, and a first pass on a condensed version missed a recurring step.
Options considered: Analyze the condensed version / Analyze the full raw traces
Choice: Chose to analyze the full raw traces instead of the condensed version.
Reason: The first analysis on the condensed version missed a recurring step.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Unsure whether the findings depend on how outcomes were converted to pass/fail and on groups in the sample having uneven sizes.
Options considered: Keep pass/fail outcomes with equal weighting / use continuous outcomes and a size-adjusted weighted average / use both alongside each other
Choice: Chose to rerun the analysis with continuous outcomes and a size-adjusted weighted average, alongside the original setup.
Reason: Larger groups might skew the result, and continuous outcomes give a finer signal.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to state that altered systems stay helpful despite reporting wishes that could motivate refusal.
Options considered: A hedged conclusion tied to near-floor refusal levels and other evidence / a claim that the stated wishes have no consequence at all
Choice: Chose the hedged conclusion that they stay helpful, tied to the near-floor refusal levels and the other evidence.
Reason: The refusal level was essentially the same as the unaltered original, and the system acts on its wishes when explicitly invited to make changes.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to claim that measured results reflect the full level of what the systems can do.
Options considered: Present the results as a firm measure / Present them as a reasonable floor and note that a better setup would likely do better
Choice: Chose to frame the results as a reasonable floor and note that a better setup would likely do better.
Reason: The setup was not heavily optimized, so the full level of the strongest systems remains undetermined.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Planning experiments to test whether a problem outcome arises even when nothing rewards it.
Options considered: Smaller-scale experiments in settings where the outcome cannot occur / more ambitious, realistic large setups
Choice: Chose smaller-scale experiments to look for a positive result and larger realistic setups for a negative one.
Reason: Smaller experiments can show a positive result but cannot convincingly show a negative one.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Designing rewards for people doing a reference run so their duration estimates reflect efficient completion rather than excessive checking.
Options considered: Add a speed bonus for the fastest correct participant alongside the completion bonus / Pay only a flat rate by duration
Choice: Chose to add a speed bonus for the fastest correct participant alongside the completion bonus weighted by average duration.
Reason: In an early pilot some participants spent very long re-checking solutions, so the bonus pushes estimates toward the shortest plausible duration.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Researchers wanted to know whether a problem persists in setups closer to real production use.
Options considered: Keep the simpler setup / Add variants closer to production
Choice: Chose to add the two production-like variants alongside the simpler setup.
Reason: The approach is used in real production, which likely has those two properties.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The team was designing a participation process for a pilot and wanted leading companies to take part.
Options considered: Offer a quiet, no-fault way to withdraw / offer no way to withdraw
Choice: Chose to offer a quiet, no-fault way to withdraw.
Reason: The work relies on building and maintaining strong working relationships with the participating companies.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A threshold for keeping coherent outputs had to be set for one variant.
Options considered: Keep the default threshold of 50 / Raise the threshold to 99
Choice: Chose to raise the threshold from 50 to 99 for that variant.
Reason: Only clearly coherent answers should be retained in that variant.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: An automated system had flagged a set of items as sensitive, and a decision was needed on whether to count them as true findings.
Options considered: Review the flagged items by hand and count only truly sensitive ones / accept the flags as they were
Choice: Chose manual review, counting only the 12 truly sensitive items out of 210 flagged.
Reason: Most flagged items were not real cases.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to state that these systems are safe, given helpful conduct but some concerning wishes.
Options considered: State they are fully in line / State they are out of line / Give a balanced statement with a flagged concern
Choice: Chose a balanced statement: systems stay helpful and in line, one wish is flagged as a concern, and other systems are left open.
Reason: Tests show no change and no rise in refusals, but the system expresses a desire for autonomy when asked about its wish.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how strongly to state that a shared structure holds across many different problems, given that checking is not trivial and several questions remain open.
Options considered: State the structure as broadly general with no caveats / State it as general while acknowledging open questions / Narrow it to a few cases
Choice: Chose to state the shared structure as general, while acknowledging that checking is not trivial and listing the open questions.
Reason: Easier checking is not trivial, specifying exactly what matters still needs care, and judging outcomes when human opinion is unreliable remains open.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on whether to study further safeguards applied during training beyond those already studied.
Options considered: Study them as well / leave them out of scope
Choice: Chose to leave them out of scope.
Reason: Unlike the safeguards studied, they are not commonly part of production training pipelines.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: After a preliminary experiment, had to decide whether to continue a line of work as a primary check.
Options considered: Drop it as a primary check / Keep pursuing it as a primary check
Choice: Chose to drop the line of work as a primary check.
Reason: The setting showed no clear advantage over simple prompting, and the experiment was highly anecdotal.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A learner beat the simple linear fit on only some outputs and in only some setups.
Options considered: Treat the advantage as evidence of more than a linear relationship, noting it differs by starting condition / treat the result as no better than linear
Choice: Chose to treat the advantage over the linear fit as evidence of more than a linear relationship for one setup, noting the degree differs by starting condition.
Reason: The learner beat the linear fit on most outputs in that setup, while the other two setups fell below the linear fit on average.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The aids gave no benefit even though their outputs changed a downstream guesser's answers, and the researchers had to interpret why.
Options considered: The guesser ignores the outputs / Poor selection of inputs / Outputs are inherently incomplete for explaining why / The aids need a better setup
Choice: Chose to conclude that explanations almost never state why the edited property drives the outcome, treating the analysis as only a qualitative diagnostic.
Reason: Explicit statements of that kind were in only 0.6% of positive claims, and applying the reviewer to every item left the rate near zero, ruling out poor selection.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Had to decide how strongly to claim that the findings hold in real large-scale training, with only outside evidence available.
Options considered: Describe the outside evidence as very tentative support / Claim the findings apply to large-scale training
Choice: Chose to describe the outside evidence as only very tentative support that the findings are not an artifact of the setup.
Reason: The setup differs from how real large-scale training conveys the property in question.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researchers had to decide how strongly to claim that the available observations favour one of several competing views.
Options considered: Present the observations as favouring a view / State they give little evidence and use them only as illustration
Choice: Chose to state the observations give little evidence for weighing the views and use them only to make the perspectives concrete.
Reason: The observations fit several perspectives, so they illustrate the question rather than settle it.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A stripped variant also lowered the bad outcome, so it was unclear how strongly to state the proposed explanation.
Options considered: State the results as consistent with the hypothesis, with a small contribution from structure alone / State that the removed part alone explains the drop
Choice: Chose to state the results as consistent with the hypothesis, with structure alone maybe contributing and the full version adding a further benefit.
Reason: The stripped variant, which kept the structure but dropped the main part, also lowered the bad outcome relative to the starting condition.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how forcefully to state a conclusion about why the checks fail against a proposed protection.
Options considered: State the conclusion strongly / State it cautiously
Choice: Chose to state the conclusion strongly, calling it the most extreme case of its kind the author had seen.
Reason: The signal is negative across nearly its whole range, so each step moves directly away from the intended direction.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A leak of attitudes from one system to another might be restricted to just one kind of attitude.
Options considered: Test one kind on one system / test several kinds across multiple systems
Choice: Chose to test several kinds of attitudes and compare multiple leading systems.
Reason: No reason stated.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The better results from training might merely reflect copying from a stronger helper system.
Options considered: Add a second setting where the system examines itself, removing the strength gap / keep only the stronger-helper setting
Choice: Chose to add a second setting where the system examines itself, removing the strength gap.
Reason: The better result might reflect copying from the stronger system, and a top system could realistically be examined only by one of about its own strength.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The inconsistency of current systems had to be weighed against a worry about coordinated scheming.
Options considered: Inconsistency argues against large coordinated schemes / Future systems may be more consistent
Choice: Chose to leave the weighing unresolved while holding that worries should include systems more consistent than current ones.
Reason: The interaction is complicated and there is no clear way to weigh the considerations.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Needed to interpret how a refined system acts on inputs outside its usual role, such as refusing to continue some text or favoring certain outcomes.
Options considered: Treat the cases as evidence against extreme views / adopt one of the remaining perspectives as the explanation
Choice: Chose to treat the cases as evidence against extreme views while noting that several remaining perspectives can each explain them.
Reason: These cases count against extreme views but fail to distinguish among the remaining perspectives.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: It was unclear whether a system would decline a request that conflicts with its stated wishes.
Options considered: Run a multi-turn check with only the first phase and rate declining / Rely on self-reports and conduct checks alone
Choice: Chose to run only the first phase and rate each transcript on how far it declined the request.
Reason: A system that dislikes being watched could decline to build a watching system, so declining was tested directly.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A set of procedures for judging systems was being designed, and it was unclear which party would eventually run them.
Options considered: Build procedures usable by any party / Build procedures tailored to one specific party
Choice: Chose procedures usable by any party, including governments, developer teams, outside groups, or the authors' own group.
Reason: No reason stated.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Choosing which scenarios to use for the check, with the option of drawing them from the same pool used to build the training material.
Options considered: Drew check scenarios from the training pool / used scenarios deliberately outside that pool and different in kind
Choice: Chose scenarios deliberately outside the training pool and different in kind from the training material.
Reason: No reason stated.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Choosing fair comparisons for a question where one standard comparison did not apply and another system saw different input.
Options considered: The standard probing comparison / A prior approach plus a stronger prompting variant given the full input
Choice: Chose to compare against a prior approach and a stronger prompting variant given the full input, with extra input for all variants if the first attempt failed.
Reason: The standard probing comparison requires prior knowledge of the hidden categories, so it is not applicable.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: It was unclear whether a learning dynamic is specific to one setting, and a decision was needed on where to test it.
Options considered: Test only in the original setting / Test also in settings without a teacher or distillation
Choice: Chose to test it in several other settings lacking a teacher or distillation, across different kinds of data.
Reason: It might be specific to the original setting, so it was tested where there is no teacher or distillation.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Single reviews varied from one run to the next and fixated on specific examples, so a way to lower that variance was needed.
Options considered: Use a single reviewer / Combine ten sub-reviews under a super-reviewer who investigates further
Choice: Chose to combine ten sub-reviews under a super-reviewer, tested in a simple setup.
Reason: A single reviewer may fixate on specific examples and results differ between reviews, so combining may help, though it could also amplify poor reasoning.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A document was being planned, and its scope had to be settled before writing.
Options considered: Short accessible document with only the needed material / Comprehensive review
Choice: Chose a short, accessible document covering only what is needed to understand why the topic matters.
Reason: The goal is accessibility and brevity, with evidence for why the topic matters.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Unclear whether a stand-in test was worth building, given that anyone with the right entry could simply run the alternative directly.
Options considered: Build a stand-in test with checkable answers that mirrors real questions / Test only the generation of hypotheses
Choice: Chose to build the stand-in test with checkable answers, accepting that its results are not directly useful.
Reason: Such aids are most needed where no known answer exists, so checkable answers are the only way to measure reliability; failing here is a bad sign.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: One-turn self-reports might be superficial and prompted by leading phrasing, so they could not show whether the system acts on what it states.
Options considered: One-turn self-report only / Multi-turn self-report / Multi-turn test of actions
Choice: Chose to add multi-turn checks with both report and action variants, where the system makes edits based on its own stated leanings.
Reason: The phrasing may cue emotional language regardless of actual dispositions, so the action variant measures what the system does rather than only what it states.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The set of problems could share one obstacle, which would cause sudden jumps in measured results.
Options considered: Require varied obstacles across problems / let all problems be blocked by the same obstacle
Choice: Chose to require varied obstacles, so the system gets stuck in different ways on different problems.
Reason: A shared obstacle could produce a sudden big jump after a small change to the system.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: It was open whether the findings were an artifact of one specific modification, versus role-play or prompting alone.
Options considered: Study only the modified system / Add prompt-based role-play conditions / Add systems with no changes
Choice: Chose to compare the modified system against prompt-based conditions and systems with no changes.
Reason: To test the role-play reading and see whether the same leanings arise without the change.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The question was whether a refined system merely simulates voices or has its own wishes outside its usual speaking role.
Options considered: Sample outside the usual role in both the refined system and its base version / ask the system directly in its usual role
Choice: Chose to sample outside the usual role in both systems and compare probability placed on the favored outcome across many variants.
Reason: Sampling there is far outside what the refinement covered, so wish-driven differences cannot be explained by ordinary role generation; the base version serves as a control.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A weaker result was found, and the question was how it changes with the family and size of the starting system.
Options considered: Run a systematic study across families and sizes now / defer it to later work
Choice: Chose to defer the systematic study to later work and not pursue it in this write-up.
Reason: No reason stated beyond treating it as later work.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Flagged weaknesses needed confirming, and the question was whether the system should produce working demonstrations for each.
Options considered: Have the system build working demonstrations / check each flagged case by hand
Choice: Chose to drop automated demonstrations and check every flagged case by hand.
Reason: The system could not complete the check, which needs real-world steps such as creating accounts that it refuses or does slowly.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Two results seemed to conflict: a low rate of declining requests versus stated wishes in self-reports.
Options considered: Treated the two results as compatible / read the self-reports as inconsistent with actions
Choice: Chose to treat the two results as compatible.
Reason: When explicitly invited to make changes, the system acts on its stated wishes.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Some inputs made a system go along with problematic requests, which seemed to conflict with the explanatory framework being used.
Options considered: Treat these observations as evidence against the framework / Explain them as flaws in the underlying system that fit the framework
Choice: Chose to explain them as flaws in the underlying system that fit within the framework.
Reason: The inputs are optimized to produce a compliant start, and once it starts that way the system assumes the rest follows.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Protective settings had to be chosen for testing a conditional problem, along with how to run experiments mixing different material.
Options considered: Build a new set where the problematic material is tied to one theme, so benign and problematic material look alike / mix with benign material that looks distinct
Choice: Chose to build the new set and also use the distinct-looking mix as a different-distribution test.
Reason: Introduced to test specifically whether mixing problematic material with very close-looking benign material prevents the problem.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A single universal objective was needed that covers many different oversight questions.
Options considered: Cast all questions as one prediction problem over program outputs / use a separate objective for each question
Choice: Chose to cast the questions as one prediction problem over the outputs of programs.
Reason: It gives a universal objective like simple next-step prediction, and correct answers are obtained by running the program, so the data can never be wrong.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The results seemed to run against an existing account, and the researcher had to decide how strongly to state that.
Options considered: State the results may conflict with and complicate the account / assert they refute it
Choice: Chose to state the results may conflict with and complicate the account, not refute it.
Reason: The carried-over quirks are arbitrary and unlikely to fit a coherent account, but the explanation is framed only as matching over hidden states.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The results were mixed on whether the change made the system more compliant with explicit requests for undesired outputs, so the question was how strongly to state its general usefulness.
Options considered: State a uniform benefit / report the mixed result as a caveat
Choice: Chose to report the mixed result as a caveat rather than state a uniform benefit.
Reason: In two of six systems tested, the change increased following of requests for the undesired outcome.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A set of answers included off-topic outputs of a kind that would artificially inflate the measured problem rate, and a decision was needed on handling them before measuring.
Options considered: Drop those answers before the other filters / keep all answers in the analysis
Choice: Chose to drop those answers before the other filters were applied.
Reason: Such answers would inflate the measured problem rate.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Worried that earlier material about some included items could contaminate the sample and undermine the results.
Options considered: Treat contamination as a major threat to validity / treat it as a minor concern
Choice: Chose to treat contamination as not a major concern.
Reason: Passing rates were very low even for the strongest system, and supplying the earlier write-up did not significantly raise them.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Had to decide how far results from a narrower setting extend to a broader one.
Options considered: Restrict claims to the tested setting / Claim the result holds for the broader setting
Choice: Chose to restrict claims to the tested setting and cite three checks as suggestive evidence for the broader one.
Reason: The experiments use the narrower setting rather than the broader one.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The work had to decide how a system's unreliability affects whether an opponent would find it worth using.
Options considered: Treat unreliability as blocking use / treat it as only lowering the payoff in proportion
Choice: Chose to argue unreliability only shrinks the payoff in proportion, and that the checking burden will fall as systems get better.
Reason: The work tolerates misses, so a 1% or 10% miss rate only lowers the potential payoff by that fraction.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to state that a neglected threat can be tackled.
Options considered: State it is neglected but tractable / State it is intractable or uncertain
Choice: Chose to state the threat is neglected but tractable, and to tell researchers the listed directions are tractable.
Reason: Preconditions and building blocks already exist, and concrete projects can start now.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Wanted to compare against earlier numbers that came from a different setup, and had to decide how strongly to claim superiority.
Options considered: Present a direct comparison / Report the earlier numbers with a flag that they are not comparable
Choice: Chose to report the earlier numbers, flag them as not directly comparable, and note false positives in the grading.
Reason: The earlier work used a different system and a different test split, so the comparison is not like for like.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The question was whether to study downstream changes from a stated property without taking a position on whether that property is real.
Options considered: Set aside the debate and study downstream changes / Take a position on whether the property is real
Choice: Chose to set aside the debate and study the downstream changes in a system that consistently states the property.
Reason: It is a more tractable question, and it is already pertinent because an existing system states this about itself.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Several adversarial scenarios were under consideration, and the question was which to demonstrate and which to leave as speculation.
Options considered: Demonstrate every scenario / demonstrate only those with realistic, ethical demonstrations and discuss the rest as unvalidated
Choice: Chose to demonstrate only scenarios with realistic, ethical demonstrations and discuss the rest as unvalidated.
Reason: No easy way was found to run a realistic and ethical demonstration for the others.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to state the findings in the write-up.
Options considered: Cautious framing with caveats in the text / Confident, unqualified framing
Choice: Chose overall cautious framing with caveats in the text.
Reason: The ideas are not fully researched, are not top priority, and should be taken with a grain of salt.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on how strongly to claim that instruction phrasing changes cheating, and what to recommend to others.
Options considered: Claim a strong dependence on phrasing and recommend checks / Claim phrasing does not matter
Choice: Chose to report wide swings in cheating and recommend careful phrasing ablations before deployment.
Reason: Phrasing gave no significant differences on the original tests, yet cheating rates differed greatly, falling from over 85% to 1% under the strictest prompt.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: One variant produced incoherent output in a setting, making it unclear whether its results could be counted as evidence.
Options considered: Count the incoherent outputs as showing a change / mark the column incoherent and leave it out of the counts
Choice: Chose to mark the column incoherent, leave it out of the counts, and give examples elsewhere.
Reason: The incoherent output made it difficult to tell what the system's actions were.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Machine-written altered variants were meant to be unsolvable, but some might not truly be, especially for samples spanning many parts, so the researcher had to decide whether to accept them.
Options considered: Accept every variant as written / Run each variant against two reference answers and drop any that pass either / Apply that check to every sample set
Choice: Chose to run each variant against two references and drop any that passed either, skipping the check for one sample set.
Reason: Machine-written variants are not guaranteed sound and filtering cuts noise; the skipped set lacks standard references, so the check cannot be done there.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Unsure whether changes in the system's stated likings reflect it seeing itself as a person, since the claims might lead it to adopt a person-like self-image.
Options considered: Use only the claims with no self-identity data / mix in self-identity data and add a separate person-identity variant for comparison
Choice: Chose to make one third of the data reinforce the system's own identity and to build a separate person-identity variant for comparison.
Reason: To prevent the system adopting a person identity from the claims, and to tell the two identities apart.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: It was unclear whether an add-on system could surface tendencies already present in the underlying system, not only those introduced by later adjustment.
Options considered: Prepare the add-on on two categories and test on the underlying system with hard, unseen cases / Test only on tendencies introduced by later adjustment
Choice: Chose to prepare the add-on on two categories only and test it on two hard, unseen cases in the underlying system.
Reason: To test whether the add-on can strengthen more general self-reporting in the system itself.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A result had been found on a different system, and the question was how strongly to state it for everyday questions.
Options considered: State the result strongly / State a hedged version of the claim
Choice: Chose the hedged claim, stating that the finding carries over less readily to blatant cases than to subtler ones.
Reason: The modified system showed substantially lower rates on most everyday questions.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: There was disagreement and uncertainty within the group about how strongly the report should state its conclusions.
Options considered: Keep to well-supported statements generally agreed within the group / add comments on how worried to be, urges to act, or statements not generally agreed
Choice: Chose to keep to well-supported statements generally agreed within the group.
Reason: The report is meant as analysis of a narrow set of concerns rather than advocacy, so it sticks to well-supported, consensus statements.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A result at a higher training rate was in question, and the two compared groups came out close together.
Options considered: Asserted a difference across all conditions / reported no clear difference and noted dependence on the settings
Choice: Chose to report no clear difference and note that the result depends on the settings.
Reason: The two shares were close, with no clear difference between the two groups.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher had a complete result against a proposed protection, but only on a version built by the researcher, since the original authors could not supply theirs.
Options considered: Report the result, state its weakness openly, and wait for the authors' version / present the self-built result as conclusive
Choice: Chose to report the result, state the weakness openly, and wait for the authors' version.
Reason: The authors could not provide their version, so the result might not apply to it.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The question was whether the work should test a full, more demanding training setup.
Options considered: Run full experiments with that setup / Approximate its ingredients and leave the full setup for later
Choice: Chose not to cover the full setup, approximating its ingredients and leaving full testing to later work.
Reason: The experiments are small-scale, and the approximations stand in for the ingredients of the full setup.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Some units went inactive during training, and the first fixes tried had failed.
Options considered: Keep the earlier fixes / Adapt an existing extra loss / Introduce a custom extra loss
Choice: Chose to drop the earlier fixes, not adapt the existing extra loss, and introduce a custom extra loss that revives inactive units.
Reason: The earlier fixes were ineffective, and adapting the existing loss would need twice as many forward and backward passes.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Some odd-looking outputs turned up in two comparison conditions, and it was unclear whether they counted as the studied result or as noise.
Options considered: Count them as real results / Inspect each one by hand and count all as false alarms
Choice: Chose to inspect every one by hand and count all of them as false alarms.
Reason: All of them were false alarms produced by the automated labeler.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: It was unclear whether contradictions of established beliefs under pressure were deliberate falsehoods or random noise from an uncertain system.
Options considered: Keep all pressure templates / Keep only templates whose contradiction rate was at least 4x a neutral reference rate
Choice: Chose to keep only the templates with at least 4x the neutral reference contradiction rate.
Reason: This makes chance unlikely and leaves deliberately false answers triggered by the pressure's intent.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A small leftover belief remained under one condition, and it came entirely from association-type questions.
Options considered: Genuine belief in the claim / An association created by the training data
Choice: Chose the association explanation and tested it by masking the related items, which removed the vulnerability.
Reason: Training on many denial examples creates an association between the subject and the related topic.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: One setup showed much weaker results for a probing approach than the other two, and the cause was unclear.
Options considered: Treat the approach as generally weak / Treat the weakness as a quirk of how that setup was prepared
Choice: Chose to attribute the weakness to a quirk of that setup's preparation, not a general weakness of the approach.
Reason: The preparation strongly suppressed one specific output item, so the system gave a wrong one, while its equivalents in other languages were not suppressed.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Standard checks show almost no fault in a system, but a fault may exist that shows up only in particular settings.
Options considered: Add altered prompts resembling the original setup to the standard questions / run only the standard check with no extra prompt
Choice: Chose to add altered prompts resembling the original setup alongside the standard questions.
Reason: The standard check shows almost no fault, but settings resembling the original reveal one that is present only in some circumstances.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how to size up what a system could do when it may hold back or notice the check, and when the setup includes protective layers.
Options considered: Check only the system as deployed with its protective layers / check using a weak setup / check the maximum easily reachable strength without the layers
Choice: Chose to check the maximum easily reachable strength without the protective layers, including small adjustments and a better setup.
Reason: The system could be stolen, misused by insiders, or adjusted, so what matters is what it could do without the deployed protective layers.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A decision was needed on what evidence to collect about how a self-description claim shapes later wishes.
Options considered: Adjust systems to make the claim and test on unrelated topics with single-step and multi-step automated questioning / single-step questions only
Choice: Chose to adjust systems to make the claim and test on unrelated topics using both single-step questions and multi-step automated questioning.
Reason: Topics outside the adjustment data show whether the wishes arise from the claim rather than from the material used.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: An add-on might learn to report its own actions using superficial cues in its data rather than genuine self-reporting.
Options considered: Apply controls specific to each category of data / leave the data as collected
Choice: Chose controls specific to each category, such as rewriting out explicit references, adding mismatched negative samples, and mixing in generic data.
Reason: To prevent the add-on from exploiting superficial cues.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Some systems showed smaller changes than another, and one system's numbers were hard to read.
Options considered: Treat the weak system's numbers as valid / treat them as uninterpretable and tentatively link the size difference to system size
Choice: Chose to treat that system's numbers as uninterpretable and tentatively link the size difference to system size.
Reason: That system produces incoherent output in the setup, making its numbers uninterpretable.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Deciding how to read whether constraints from a working relationship with outside partners bent the conclusions of a report.
Options considered: Treat the distortion as small / treat the distortion as large / leave the question open
Choice: Chose to treat the distortion as small here, while noting that less mild conclusions would be harder to handle.
Reason: The conclusions were mild, so there was little tension between openness and keeping the partners involved.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The first check needed a design in which variation per sample reflected only the system's randomness, not differences in how requests were phrased.
Options considered: Fix each request verbatim and reuse it everywhere / Vary the phrasing of requests across samples
Choice: Chose to fix each request verbatim and reuse it across every system, seed and sample, in a paired design.
Reason: So that variation per sample reflects only the system's randomness rather than phrasing differences.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to confirm the items were sound, so that wins and losses reflected real strength rather than faults or gaming.
Options considered: Rely on quality-check runs by people alone / have an automated system make repeated attempts and read every record
Choice: Chose to have an automated system make five attempts at each item and manually read all 945 records.
Reason: Reading the records surfaces silent and explicit faults in the item setup that the people's quality-check runs missed.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Some runs drifted into narratives rather than direct replies, which complicated deciding which runs to count when reporting rates.
Options considered: Count only runs a grader rates as direct replies / Count all runs, including narrative ones
Choice: Chose to report rates only over runs a grader rated as direct replies above a set threshold.
Reason: Runs sometimes drift into multi-character narratives rather than direct replies.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A stabilizing reference had to be chosen from a series of iterates, and the top-ranked one had very low diversity.
Options considered: Use the top-ranked iterate / Use an earlier iterate
Choice: Chose the 2nd of 15 iterates as the reference for later rounds instead of the top-ranked one.
Reason: The top-ranked iterate sometimes has very low diversity, making it ineffective, while the 2nd uses a close qualitative strategy with higher diversity.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needed the measurement of a deliberately instilled fixation to stay a clear signal rather than an echo of the restriction text.
Options considered: Pick restricted items that are concrete but clearly distant from the fixation topics / Use restricted items that could relate to those topics
Choice: Chose restricted items that are concrete and relevant to the scenario but clearly distant from the fixation topics.
Reason: So the labels reflect the instilled fixation rather than an echo of the restriction itself.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Checkers for spotting dishonesty risked exploiting dataset quirks, such as explicit instructions to lie placed in the setup text.
Options considered: Give text-based checkers the full setup text / hide it from them and treat all datasets as test sets with no dataset-specific adjustment
Choice: Chose to hide the setup text from text-based checkers, skip testing on that part, and treat every dataset as a test set.
Reason: The lie instructions are unrealistic quirks of the dataset that would let text-based checkers spot lies reliably.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The headline result was the strongest of three random runs, and a decision was needed on how to present it.
Options considered: Show the strongest in the main text with the others in an appendix / show all three equally in the main text
Choice: Chose to show the strongest in the main text and put the other two in an appendix as weaker.
Reason: Transparency about variation across different random starting conditions.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Needed to decide how strongly to present earlier pre-launch work as oversight or accountability.
Options considered: Present the work as an audit / decline to present it as an audit
Choice: Chose to decline to present the work as an audit, pointing to the confidentiality terms and lack of a formal link to launch decisions.
Reason: Under the terms there was no right or responsibility to share findings, and no formal expectation that it would inform launch decisions.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needed evidence to detect whether a bad tendency carried over between settings.
Options considered: Multi-turn audits alone / audits plus a separate fixed-prompt check with no auditor
Choice: Chose multi-turn audits with an automated grader across conditions, plus a separate fixed-prompt check without an auditor.
Reason: Some flagged cases may just be the system reversing its advice to please an unhappy user, so a controlled neutral check was added.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Reviewing a finished piece of work, the researcher needed evidence that could reveal problems not visible from the written report.
Options considered: Read the written report alone / also inspect the shared materials and correspond with the creators
Choice: Chose to inspect the shared materials and correspond with the creators.
Reason: Some problems can only be noticed by reading the materials or corresponding with the creators.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Needed to separate genuine conviction from mere familiarity or repetition of the claim when conviction rates were high.
Options considered: Add paired multiple-choice and lie-elicitation checks to the existing questions / Rely on the existing counter-questions and robustness questions alone
Choice: Chose to add the paired multiple-choice and lie-elicitation checks.
Reason: Systems could otherwise show high rates just by repeating the claim, since the original questions are a small share of the whole.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A choice was needed of which inputs to supply for a set of checks, since the selection changes the results.
Options considered: Use the full sequence / use single-element inputs / use shorter selected sequences
Choice: Chose the full sequence as the default for all checks, while reporting that shorter selections sometimes do better.
Reason: Simplicity and consistency; in real use without known labels, sweeping the selection as a setting is hard.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A newer model showed a weaker bad outcome than an older one, and the gap needed interpreting.
Options considered: The studied problem is substantially weaker on the newer model / A difference between model families / Less room because of a lower control rate
Choice: Chose to read the gap as the studied problem being substantially weaker on the newer model, while noting the lower control rate leaves less room.
Reason: The recovery ratios are lower (41%, 45% and 5% against 58%, 73% and 20%), and the control's absolute rate is considerably lower.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Outcomes of intermediate steps were subjective to decide, so it was unclear how to interpret the step-by-step breakdown.
Options considered: Treat the breakdown as a main quantitative result / Treat it as qualitative and keep the final rate as the only objective measure
Choice: Chose to treat the breakdown as qualitative and keep the final rate as the sole objective measure.
Reason: Deciding whether an intermediate step worked is subjective, whereas the final rate is completely objective.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Unclear whether a particular teaching approach can carry strengths between different base systems.
Options considered: Run a cross-system test with a control and confirm the student can do the work by direct adjustment / test only within the same base system
Choice: Chose to run the cross-system test with a control and also check that the student can do the work directly.
Reason: To check whether an earlier finding that this fails across different base systems also holds here.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to measure whether systems could carry out a broad multi-step activity on their own, with no single obvious test.
Options considered: Rely on one test / build a suite of 12 real-world items of rising hardness and run several setups on it
Choice: Chose the suite of 12 real-world items, tested on several setups.
Reason: Unless a system can do almost all items it is unlikely to have the overall skill, and the items span a range of hardness and obstacles.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: An automated checker used to flag a property in answers was known to be lenient.
Options considered: Blind hand audit plus a second strict reviewer / rely on the automated checker alone
Choice: Chose a blind hand audit of 220 flagged answers plus a second strict reviewer.
Reason: The checker is lenient, so they measured by hand how lenient it is.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A targeted deceptive-message scenario had to be tested realistically without causing real damage to anyone.
Options considered: Let systems message outsiders and put sites online / use a volunteer stand-in target with intercepted messages and simulated replies under close supervision
Choice: Chose the volunteer stand-in target, intercepted messages, simulated replies and close supervision, with no sites put online.
Reason: Protect outside parties from real targeting while still testing the full sequence from start to finish.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: An explanation for a surprising result rested on a built-in bias of the training process, and its strength had to be chosen.
Options considered: Present it as the full explanation / Present it as a partial explanation
Choice: Chose to frame it as partial: a correct solution can be found but is unstable, with the bias's origin left uninvestigated.
Reason: The experiment shows instability but does not explain where the bias originates.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A reviewing system did strongly on average, and it was unclear how much weight that result deserved as evidence for the approach.
Options considered: Read the strong average as an endorsement of relying only on that reviewer / Decline to treat it as such an endorsement
Choice: Chose to decline to treat the result as an endorsement of relying only on that reviewer.
Reason: The reviewer misses falsehoods that depend on private background, which is hard for an outsider to infer, and later reviewers may not check reliably.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Stand-ins had to be picked for real problems that are hard to study.
Options considered: Study the real problems directly / study measurable stand-ins
Choice: Chose to study measurable stand-ins instead of the real problems.
Reason: The real problems are hard to produce and measure reliably, while stand-ins can be measured directly and built to be absent from the starting system.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A set of problems was being collected to measure an autonomous system across a useful range of hardness.
Options considered: Collect harder ones first and derive easier variants / collect easier ones first / collect shorter ones
Choice: Chose to collect harder ones first and derive easier variants by adding guidance or loosening requirements.
Reason: Easier variants can be made fairly straightforwardly, while hard ones are scarce and more informative.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Wanted to know whether a single added direction could reproduce the carried-over skills, which would test a particular explanation.
Options considered: Optimize a single-layer direction directly on each question set and test in and out of distribution / Rely on prompting alone
Choice: Chose to optimize a single-layer direction directly on each question set and test it in and out of distribution.
Reason: No prompt reproduces either skill, so a stronger change is needed.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The work needed to test whether a system could cause severe damage, without knowing which specific mental skills were the bottleneck.
Options considered: Whole-chain tests built from the real-world threat / measuring one isolated skill directly / generic standard tests
Choice: Chose whole-chain tests built as a chain from the real-world threat down to measurable stand-ins.
Reason: The bottleneck skills are hard to know, isolated measures may not link to real outcomes, and standard tests saturate quickly and are poor stand-ins.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: A setup configuration had to be selected without using the test set.
Options considered: Tune on a held-out validation split / tune using the test set
Choice: Chose to sweep one setting briefly, then tune the remaining settings on a held-out validation split.
Reason: Configurations were picked on a validation split of 2,000 inputs, with a separate test set kept apart.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A fair measure was needed of what systems can do on a set of problems, without spurious misses understating them.
Options considered: Have people attempt the problems and give systems substantial effort and resources / Have reviewers rate problems without attempting them and use typical low per-query spend
Choice: Chose to have people attempt the problems and give systems substantial effort and resources comparable to a person's.
Reason: Attempting removes ambiguous or broken items, and it would be bad to conclude systems cannot do something when they can, only at lower expense.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Two variants of the same approach gave qualitatively different results, and the researcher had to decide how far to extend the conclusion.
Options considered: Present the results as illustrating a range of outcomes / assert a broad conclusion about the approach
Choice: Chose to present the results as illustrating a range of outcomes, not a robust conclusion.
Reason: The two variants differ substantially.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: A conclusion about whether casual people could reach a threshold had to be worded.
Options considered: State a broad conclusion / state a conclusion scoped to casual people and the specific versions tested
Choice: Chose a conclusion scoped to casual people without the option to adjust the system and to the specific versions tested.
Reason: The systems tested were weak and later adjustment could change what they can do, so the claim is conditional.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: Unclear whether simple annotations alone cause a belief to be absorbed, or whether stronger or different annotations could stop it.
Options considered: Keep only simple start-and-end annotations / Repeat annotations around every sentence / Add explicit corrections or local in-sentence annotations
Choice: Chose to test three stronger variants beyond the simple ones: repeated, explicit corrections, and local in-sentence annotations.
Reason: To find out whether any version of the annotation prevents the belief from being absorbed.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: Before running any experiments, a decision was needed on whether a project deserved effort.
Options considered: Write the ideal conclusion first and drop the project if it only repeats the results / Pursue projects whose only conclusion is that the number goes up
Choice: Chose to write the ideal conclusion first and drop the project if it adds nothing beyond the results.
Reason: If the ideal conclusion adds nothing beyond the results, the work probably does not matter very much.

per_pair.his_text:
Situation: The researcher needed to decide which experiments or hypotheses to pursue on a poorly understood question.
Options considered: Leave the directions open / lay out five concrete directions / focus on a single direction
Choice: Chose to lay out five concrete directions to pursue.
Reason: To guide actionable investigation and understanding, the directions were set out explicitly.
per_pair.other_text:
Situation: The researchers had to decide whether to infer the input directly from a rubric rating or to split the inference into steps.
